Accessible charts

Source: vignettes/accessibility.Rmd
accessibility.Rmd

Navigate a line chart with the keyboard

Highcharter includes the Highcharts accessibility module in the shared bundle. Give the chart a title and identify the units on its axes. Use the caption for the takeaway and the point description for details when navigating the series. Keep a distinct marker or dash style when several series use color.

highchart() |>
  hc_title(text = "Daily bicycle trips") |>
  hc_xAxis(categories = c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed"), title = list(text = "Day")) |>
  hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "Trips")) |>
  hc_add_series(data = c(24, 35, 30), name = "North route") |>
  hc_add_series(
    data = c(18, 28, 26),
    name = "South route",
    dashStyle = "Dash",
    marker = list(symbol = "diamond")
  ) |>
  hc_caption(text = "Both routes had the most trips on Tuesday.") |>
  hc_chart(animation = FALSE) |>
  hc_plotOptions(series = list(animation = FALSE)) |>
  hc_accessibility(
    enabled = TRUE,
    landmarkVerbosity = "one",
    point = list(valueDescriptionFormat = "{xDescription}, {value} trips."),
    keyboardNavigation = list(enabled = TRUE)
  ) |>
  hc_exporting(enabled = TRUE, showTable = TRUE)

Use Tab to reach the chart, the arrow keys to explore points, and Tab again to reach the legend and export controls. The HTML data table offers the values in reading order. Give every interactive chart a visible focus indicator. For a longer explanation, reference an adjacent paragraph by its unique CSS selector in hc_accessibility(linkedDescription = "#route-summary"). Use screenReaderSection to customize the text before or after the chart.

For Maps, name each region or point and include the unit in its value description. For Stock, identify the financial instrument and date. See the Maps and Stock examples. The example above disables introductory animations. The home example respects reduced motion and lets readers select either measurement. Sonification is available through hc_sonification() for readers who choose to play the chart.

Highcharts accessibility guide

A patterned pie chart

Mara Averick adapted the Highcharts accessible pie chart for highcharter and shared it in issue #736. Her design gives each slice a distinct pattern and labels it with the reader’s name and percentage. Mara’s original example on RPubs.

The values come from WebAIM’s 2019 screen reader survey. “Other” groups the four smallest responses. Tab to the pie and use the arrow keys to hear each slice’s name and survey share with a screen reader.

reader_slice <- function(name, share, color, path) {
  list(
    name = name,
    y = share,
    color = list(
      pattern = list(
        path = path,
        color = color,
        width = 5,
        height = 5,
        patternTransform = "scale(1.4 1.4)"
      )
    )
  )
}

highchart() |>
  hc_title(text = "Primary desktop/laptop screen readers") |>
  hc_subtitle(text = "WebAIM Screen Reader User Survey, 2019") |>
  hc_caption(
    text = "NVDA (40.6%) and JAWS (40.1%) were the most common responses."
  ) |>
  hc_add_series(
    type = "pie",
    name = "Screen reader usage",
    data = list(
      reader_slice(
        "NVDA",
        40.6,
        "#49a65e",
        "M 0 0 L 5 5 M 4.5 -0.5 L 5.5 0.5 M -0.5 4.5 L 0.5 5.5"
      ),
      reader_slice(
        "JAWS",
        40.1,
        "#5f98cf",
        "M 0 5 L 5 0 M -0.5 0.5 L 0.5 -0.5 M 4.5 5.5 L 5.5 4.5"
      ),
      reader_slice("VoiceOver", 12.9, "#f45b5b", "M 2 0 L 2 5 M 4 0 L 4 5"),
      reader_slice("ZoomText/Fusion", 2, "#434348", "M 0 2 L 5 2 M 0 4 L 5 4"),
      reader_slice(
        "Other",
        4.4,
        "#708090",
        "M 0 1.5 L 2.5 1.5 L 2.5 0 M 2.5 5 L 2.5 3.5 L 5 3.5"
      )
    ),
    borderWidth = 3,
    dataLabels = list(
      enabled = TRUE,
      connectorColor = "#777",
      format = "{point.name}: {point.y:.1f}%"
    )
  ) |>
  hc_tooltip(valueSuffix = "%", borderColor = "#8ae") |>
  hc_accessibility(
    point = list(valueDescriptionFormat = "{point.name}, {point.y}%.")
  ) |>
  hc_exporting(enabled = TRUE)

Screen readers and sound

Accessibility does not make a chart play sound automatically. A screen reader speaks its descriptions when you navigate to the chart. Sonification is a separate, opt-in way of listening to the values as musical notes.

highchart() |>
  hc_title(text = "Listen to the weekly pattern") |>
  hc_xAxis(categories = c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri")) |>
  hc_add_series(name = "Trips", data = c(24, 35, 30, 42, 38)) |>
  hc_exporting(
    enabled = TRUE,
    buttons = list(contextButton = list(menuItems = list("playAsSound")))
  ) |>
  hc_sonification(enabled = TRUE, duration = 1800, masterVolume = 0.35)

Choose Play as sound in the export menu. Playback starts only after that action; it does not compete with screen-reader speech when the page opens.
